_meta.description: 105 current ratings (35 criteria x 3 regions: European Union / United States / China). Derived from docs/Transition_Barrier_Assessment.xlsx (Assessment Matrix sheet), verified 2026-08-14. `source` is free-text citation, not yet linked to a specific primary_sources[] URL in criteria_schema.json.

source_verification.verified_sources_with_url_and_locator: 88 of 95 source entries across the 35-criteria schema carry a verified url + locator, checked by hand against each primary publisher, Aug 2026. The remaining 7 are company_disclosure sources, correctly flagged with a retrieval methodology rather than a single URL, since the relevant company varies by which entity is being assessed.
source_verification.material_corrections_note: Two ratings changed during verification because US federal policy reversed in 2025: MIN-R2 (US) and OGU-R1 (US) both moved -- MIN-R2 due to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's changes to Section 30D critical-minerals sourcing requirements, and OGU-R1 due to the Congressional Review Act repeal of the EPA methane fee (Waste Emissions Charge). Neither would have been caught by re-fetching the same government page -- both were caught by searching news coverage of the policy itself. This is the argument for a distinct policy-change search step, not just a source re-fetch step.

scores.criterion: Levelised cost of renewable generation vs. new-build fossil
scores.evidence: EU utility-scale solar and onshore wind LCOE (~EUR 40-60/MWh in strong-resource markets) is at or below new-build CCGT LCOE; renewables have won the large majority of new capacity tenders since 2022
scores.source: IEA World Energy Investment 2023; IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023

scores.criterion: Levelised cost of renewable generation vs. new-build fossil
scores.evidence: Unsubsidized utility-scale solar and wind LCOE in Lazard's most recent analysis sits below new-build gas CCGT in most regions; IRA production tax credits further widen the gap
scores.source: Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy Analysis; IEA World Energy Investment 2023

scores.criterion: Levelised cost of renewable generation vs. new-build fossil
scores.evidence: China's solar and wind LCOE benefits from the world's largest manufacturing scale; renewables are cost-competitive with new coal in the large majority of provinces
scores.source: IEA World Energy Investment 2023; IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023

scores.criterion: Grid-scale storage / firming technology readiness
scores.evidence: Grid-scale battery deployment growing rapidly but curtailment already material in high-renewable-penetration markets (e.g. Germany, Spain, Italy) pending grid reinforcement
scores.source: IEA Energy Storage tracking report; ENTSO-E curtailment statistics

scores.criterion: Grid-scale storage / firming technology readiness
scores.evidence: Battery storage additions record-high but concentrated in a few states (California, Texas); interconnection queue backlogs remain a binding constraint nationally
scores.source: IEA Energy Storage tracking report; BloombergNEF Energy Storage Outlook

scores.criterion: Grid-scale storage / firming technology readiness
scores.evidence: China leads global battery storage manufacturing and deployment volume, but curtailment of wind/solar in resource-rich western provinces remains a persistent grid integration issue
scores.source: IEA Energy Storage tracking report

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on power generation
scores.evidence: EU ETS price has traded consistently in the EUR 60-90/tCO2 range through 2024-2026, exceeding the H threshold
scores.source: EEX EUA spot price series; European Commission EU ETS reporting

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on power generation
scores.evidence: No federal carbon price; state-level programmes (California cap-and-trade, RGGI) apply a moderate price only in participating states, well below the EU level
scores.source: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on power generation
scores.evidence: China national ETS covers power generation with a 2024 composite closing price ranging CNY 69-106/tonne (year-end CNY 97.49/t, approx. USD 13-14/t), rising further to CNY 66.9-97/t through the 2025 sectoral expansion period — consistently below the USD 60/tCO2 H threshold and well below the EU ETS level (EUR 70-90/t).
scores.source: Progress Report of China's National Carbon Market (2025), Ministry of Ecology and Environment via Henan provincial exchange; ICAP China National ETS tracker

scores.criterion: Renewable deployment target and permitting regime
scores.evidence: Binding 2030 renewables target under the revised Renewable Energy Directive, combined with permitting reform under REPowerEU aimed at reducing approval timelines
scores.source: European Commission REPowerEU / Renewable Energy Directive (EU) 2023/2413

scores.criterion: Renewable deployment target and permitting regime
scores.evidence: No binding federal renewable target; state-level RPS programmes vary widely; interconnection queue times remain a widely documented bottleneck exceeding 3 years in most regions
scores.source: IEA Renewables market report; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory interconnection queue studies

scores.criterion: Renewable deployment target and permitting regime
scores.evidence: China exceeded its 2030 wind and solar capacity target (1,200 GW) years ahead of schedule under binding five-year-plan targets
scores.source: National Energy Administration (China) capacity statistics

scores.criterion: Corporate and utility PPA market depth
scores.evidence: Corporate PPA market well established across Northern and Western Europe with multi-year forward contracting standard for large industrial and tech buyers
scores.source: BloombergNEF Corporate Energy Market Outlook

scores.criterion: Corporate and utility PPA market depth
scores.evidence: US is the largest corporate PPA market globally by signed volume, driven heavily by data centre and technology sector demand
scores.source: BloombergNEF Corporate Energy Market Outlook

scores.criterion: Corporate and utility PPA market depth
scores.evidence: Corporate PPA market exists and is growing but remains smaller and less standardised than the US/EU, with continued dominance of state-directed offtake structures
scores.source: BloombergNEF Corporate Energy Market Outlook; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Green hydrogen cost vs. DRI-H2 breakeven
scores.evidence: Nordic green hydrogen costs (Sweden, aided by cheap hydro/wind power and long-term renewable power contracts) are approaching but not yet at the cited DRI-H2 breakeven range; wider EU average remains further from breakeven
scores.source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review; Mission Possible Partnership Steel Transition Strategy

scores.criterion: Green hydrogen cost vs. DRI-H2 breakeven
scores.evidence: IRA Section 45V hydrogen production tax credit materially improves US green hydrogen economics in optimal wind/solar locations, but the credit's availability window has been shortened: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025) accelerated termination to projects that have not begun construction by 1 January 2028 — five years earlier than the original IRA sunset. Delivered green hydrogen cost to steel plants remains above DRI-H2 breakeven in most US regions absent the credit, and the credit's shortened runway increases execution timeline risk for projects not already under construction.
scores.source: US Treasury/IRS Section 45V final regulations (3 Jan 2025); Sidley Austin, Velaw, Baker Botts, Pillsbury legislative summaries of OBBBA Section 45V provisions

scores.criterion: Green hydrogen cost vs. DRI-H2 breakeven
scores.evidence: Chinese green hydrogen costs remain above Nordic and optimal-US levels due to less mature electrolyser supply chain economics for green (as opposed to grey/coal-based) hydrogen at scale
scores.source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Scrap steel availability (EAF route feasibility)
scores.evidence: EU scrap collection and recycling rates are relatively mature but crude steel production still runs materially above the scrap-availability threshold for full EAF conversion
scores.source: World Steel Association Steel Statistical Yearbook

scores.criterion: Scrap steel availability (EAF route feasibility)
scores.evidence: US steel industry already has one of the highest EAF shares globally (~70% of production), reflecting high domestic scrap availability
scores.source: World Steel Association Steel Statistical Yearbook; American Iron and Steel Institute

scores.criterion: Scrap steel availability (EAF route feasibility)
scores.evidence: China's steel fleet is dominated by BF-BOF production with an EAF share well below the global average; scrap availability constrained by the relative youth of the domestic steel stock
scores.source: World Steel Association Steel Statistical Yearbook; OECD Steel Market Developments

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on steel production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: EU ETS price in the effective range plus CBAM definitive-regime entry from 2026, phasing out free allocation for steel in parallel, creates the H-level combination of price and border protection
scores.source: EU CBAM Regulation 2023/956; European Commission DG CLIMA free allocation benchmarks

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on steel production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: No federal carbon price applies to steel production and no equivalent border adjustment mechanism is in force
scores.source: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on steel production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: China's national ETS was expanded in 2025 to formally include the steel sector (alongside cement and aluminium smelting), raising national coverage from ~40% to ~60%+ of emissions. However, the post-expansion carbon price (CNY 66.9-97/tonne through late 2024-2025, approx. USD 9-14/tonne) remains far below the level needed to close the green steel cost gap: analysis shows a carbon price of approximately CNY 890/tonne (~USD 124/t) would be needed for DRI-H2 cost parity at current green hydrogen prices — roughly 9x the current price and 1.6x the EU ETS level. First compliance deadline for the newly covered sectors is end-2025, covering 2024 emissions, with free allocation dominating in the initial 2024-2026 period.
scores.source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (China) allocation plan (Nov 2025); ICAP China National ETS tracker; IEEFA ETS reforms analysis; Transition Asia sector brief (Sept 2025) for the 890 yuan/t breakeven calculation

scores.criterion: Green/low-carbon steel public procurement or building-code mandate
scores.evidence: EU Green Public Procurement criteria exist and several member states have piloted embodied-carbon requirements in public construction, but a binding EU-wide mandate for steel specifically is not yet in force
scores.source: European Commission DG ENV Green Public Procurement criteria

scores.criterion: Green/low-carbon steel public procurement or building-code mandate
scores.evidence: Federal Buy Clean Initiative directs federal procurement toward lower-embodied-carbon materials including steel, but scope is limited to federal contracts rather than an economy-wide mandate
scores.source: US GSA / EPA Federal Buy Clean Initiative

scores.criterion: Green/low-carbon steel public procurement or building-code mandate
scores.evidence: No material low-carbon steel procurement mandate or building-code requirement identified in the domestic Chinese market
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review of national/provincial standards

scores.criterion: Green steel price premium and recoverability
scores.evidence: Multiple disclosed offtake agreements between European green steel producers and automotive OEMs with SBTi scope 3 commitments, at a disclosed premium
scores.source: Company investor disclosures; BloombergNEF Green Steel Tracker

scores.criterion: Green steel price premium and recoverability
scores.evidence: First Movers Coalition and SteelZero-type demand commitments exist among some US buyers but signed offtake volume at commercial scale remains limited relative to the EU
scores.source: Mission Possible Partnership Steel sector tracker; First Movers Coalition members list

scores.criterion: Green steel price premium and recoverability
scores.evidence: No material domestic green steel premium or offtake market identified; CBAM exposure affects only the exported share of Chinese steel production
scores.source: BloombergNEF Green Steel Tracker

scores.criterion: CCS capture technology deployment status
scores.evidence: A full-scale cement CCS facility in Norway is operational (~0.4 Mtpa), the first of its kind globally, establishing an operating track record
scores.source: Global CCS Institute CO2RE database; company project disclosures

scores.criterion: CCS capture technology deployment status
scores.evidence: Several cement CCS projects are in planning or FID stage under DOE Industrial Demonstrations Program support, but no full-scale facility is yet operational
scores.source: Global CCS Institute CO2RE database; US DOE Industrial Demonstrations Program

scores.criterion: CCS capture technology deployment status
scores.evidence: No full-scale operational or FID-stage cement CCS facility identified in China as of the assessment date
scores.source: Global CCS Institute CO2RE database; pending direct verification

scores.criterion: Clinker substitution rate (SCM availability)
scores.evidence: EU average clinker ratio has been declining via SCM substitution but remains above the H threshold on a region-wide basis
scores.source: Global Cement and Concrete Association sustainability data

scores.criterion: Clinker substitution rate (SCM availability)
scores.evidence: US clinker ratio broadly similar to EU average; fly ash availability declining as coal plants retire, creating a supply constraint on this specific SCM
scores.source: Global Cement and Concrete Association sustainability data; Portland Cement Association

scores.criterion: Clinker substitution rate (SCM availability)
scores.evidence: China's large cement sector has significant SCM substitution in some provinces, but sector-wide average clinker ratio data is less transparently reported than in the EU/US
scores.source: Global Cement and Concrete Association; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on cement production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: EU ETS price plus CBAM coverage of cement from the definitive regime, with free allocation phasing out in parallel
scores.source: EU CBAM Regulation 2023/956; European Commission DG CLIMA cement clinker benchmark

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on cement production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: No federal carbon price applies to cement production and no border adjustment mechanism is in force
scores.source: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on cement production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: China's national ETS was expanded in 2025 to formally include cement (alongside steel and aluminium smelting). The post-expansion carbon price (CNY 66.9-97/tonne, approx. USD 9-14/tonne) remains well below the level required to make CCS-based cement decarbonisation economically rational, and free allocation dominates for covered cement entities through the initial 2024-2026 compliance period. No CBAM-equivalent border levy applies to protect low-carbon Chinese cement producers competing domestically against unabated production.
scores.source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (China) allocation plan (Nov 2025); ICAP China National ETS tracker; IEEFA ETS reforms analysis

scores.criterion: CCS infrastructure support scheme
scores.evidence: EU Innovation Fund has made disbursed grant awards to cement CCS projects, providing a live and demonstrated funding mechanism
scores.source: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) award decisions

scores.criterion: CCS infrastructure support scheme
scores.evidence: DOE Industrial Demonstrations Program has made awards under IRA/BIL funding but disbursement to cement CCS remains at an earlier stage than the EU precedent
scores.source: US Department of Energy Industrial Demonstrations Program awards

scores.criterion: CCS infrastructure support scheme
scores.evidence: No dedicated public funding mechanism for industrial cement CCS identified at a scale comparable to the EU or US programmes
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review of NDRC programmes

scores.criterion: Low-carbon cement premium recoverability
scores.evidence: Green public procurement rules exist in several member states and international coalitions include cement/concrete demand commitments, but a binding EU-wide mandate is not yet universal
scores.source: European Commission DG ENV; First Movers Coalition Cement & Concrete commitments

scores.criterion: Low-carbon cement premium recoverability
scores.evidence: Federal Buy Clean Initiative and some state-level programmes create procurement-linked demand, though scope remains limited relative to total market
scores.source: US GSA/EPA Federal Buy Clean Initiative; California Department of General Services

scores.criterion: Low-carbon cement premium recoverability
scores.evidence: No material low-carbon cement premium recovery mechanism identified in the domestic Chinese market
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Green/blue hydrogen availability for ammonia and feedstock use
scores.evidence: EU low-carbon hydrogen cost gap to grey hydrogen has narrowed with rising EU ETS carbon price but remains material outside the most favourable renewable-resource locations
scores.source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review; IEA The Future of Petrochemicals

scores.criterion: Green/blue hydrogen availability for ammonia and feedstock use
scores.evidence: IRA Section 45V credit materially improves US low-carbon hydrogen economics for chemicals feedstock use in favourable locations, though the gap to grey hydrogen remains wide outside credit-eligible projects. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025) accelerated the credit's termination to projects not begun by 1 January 2028, shortening the window in which new chemicals-sector low-carbon hydrogen projects can secure the credit and increasing financing risk for projects not yet under construction.
scores.source: US Treasury/IRS Section 45V final regulations; IEA Global Hydrogen Review; OBBBA legislative summaries (Sidley Austin, Velaw)

scores.criterion: Green/blue hydrogen availability for ammonia and feedstock use
scores.evidence: Chinese chemicals sector remains predominantly coal- and gas-based feedstock; low-carbon hydrogen cost gap for chemical feedstock use remains wide
scores.source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Electrification of process heat (steam cracking) readiness
scores.evidence: Electric steam cracker pilot projects are at demonstration scale in Europe, representing TRL 6-7
scores.source: IEA The Future of Petrochemicals; company/consortium technical disclosures

scores.criterion: Electrification of process heat (steam cracking) readiness
scores.evidence: No comparable commercial-scale electric cracker pilot identified in the US as of the assessment date
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Electrification of process heat (steam cracking) readiness
scores.evidence: No comparable commercial-scale electric cracker pilot identified in China as of the assessment date
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on chemicals production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: EU ETS price applies to chemicals subsectors but free allocation remains material for ammonia and olefins benchmarks; chemicals not yet in CBAM scope
scores.source: European Commission DG CLIMA chemicals sector benchmarks

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on chemicals production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: No federal carbon price applies to chemicals production
scores.source: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price on chemicals production incl. border adjustment
scores.evidence: Chemicals sector not yet materially covered by China's national ETS at an effective price level
scores.source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (China) national ETS expansion roadmap

scores.criterion: Green ammonia/methanol offtake market
scores.evidence: European shipping and industrial buyers have signed early-stage green ammonia/methanol offtake agreements, driven substantially by anticipated IMO and FuelEU Maritime compliance demand
scores.source: Company investor disclosures

scores.criterion: Green ammonia/methanol offtake market
scores.evidence: US green ammonia/methanol offtake activity remains at an earlier and smaller scale than Europe's, concentrated in a small number of announced Gulf Coast projects
scores.source: Directional estimate pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Green ammonia/methanol offtake market
scores.evidence: No material green ammonia/methanol domestic offtake market identified
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Mine electrification and processing technology readiness
scores.evidence: Battery-electric mining equipment pilots operating at several European mines, though sector-wide deployment remains limited relative to the installed diesel fleet
scores.source: IEA Critical Minerals Outlook; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Mine electrification and processing technology readiness
scores.evidence: Similar pilot-stage deployment pattern to the EU; a small number of operating mines have adopted battery-electric equipment at scale
scores.source: S&P Global Market Intelligence; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Mine electrification and processing technology readiness
scores.evidence: China's domestic mining equipment manufacturing base is investing in electrification, though deployment across the very large domestic mining sector remains uneven
scores.source: IEA Critical Minerals Outlook; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Fast-track permitting regime for strategic minerals projects
scores.evidence: EU Critical Raw Materials Act establishes a statutory fast-track permitting requirement (target 27 months for Strategic Projects) that meets the H threshold
scores.source: EU Critical Raw Materials Act (Regulation 2024/1252)

scores.criterion: Fast-track permitting regime for strategic minerals projects
scores.evidence: Federal permitting reform efforts and Defense Production Act invocations have accelerated some strategic projects, but a statutory economy-wide fast-track timeline comparable to the EU CRMA is not in force
scores.source: US Department of Interior; Congressional Research Service permitting reform tracking

scores.criterion: Fast-track permitting regime for strategic minerals projects
scores.evidence: China's state-directed mining approval process for strategic minerals is generally faster than Western jurisdictions given the state's direct role in project sponsorship
scores.source: Ministry of Natural Resources (China); directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Domestic sourcing / content requirement policy
scores.evidence: EU Critical Raw Materials Act sets binding 2030 benchmarks for domestic extraction (10%), processing (40%), and recycling (25%) of strategic raw material consumption
scores.source: EU Critical Raw Materials Act (Regulation 2024/1252)

scores.criterion: Domestic sourcing / content requirement policy
scores.evidence: Section 30D's critical mineral sourcing requirement no longer functions as an active demand-side incentive: the New Clean Vehicle Credit terminated for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21, signed 4 July 2025). The domestic/FTA-partner sourcing thresholds that previously tied a material subsidy to critical mineral origin have lost their financial mechanism. Some residual effect persists through Section 45X advanced manufacturing credits and remaining IRA-era supply chain investment already committed, which is why this is a downgrade to Moderate rather than Low.
scores.source: US Department of Energy / IRS Section 30D guidance; Sidley Austin, Kirkland & Ellis, Steptoe legislative summaries of OBBBA (P.L. 119-21), all confirming Sept 30 2025 termination date

scores.criterion: Domestic sourcing / content requirement policy
scores.evidence: China applies export control measures on selected critical minerals which function as a form of domestic-sourcing/strategic-control policy, though this differs structurally from an inbound content requirement
scores.source: Ministry of Commerce (China) export control announcements

scores.criterion: Committed offtake and supply agreements vs. identified demand gap
scores.evidence: EU remains heavily import-dependent for most strategic minerals; domestic offtake agreements and committed expansion capacity cover only a small share of the identified regional supply gap
scores.source: IEA Critical Minerals Outlook regional supply gap tables

scores.criterion: Committed offtake and supply agreements vs. identified demand gap
scores.evidence: IRA-linked demand and Defense Production Act support have catalysed a growing pipeline of domestic and allied offtake agreements, though the identified NZE-scenario supply gap remains largely uncovered
scores.source: IEA Critical Minerals Outlook; company disclosures

scores.criterion: Committed offtake and supply agreements vs. identified demand gap
scores.evidence: China's dominant position in processing capacity for lithium, cobalt, and rare earths means domestic offtake and supply chain integration already covers a large share of its own demand and a material share of global demand
scores.source: IEA Critical Minerals Outlook; USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries

scores.criterion: SAF production capacity vs. jet fuel demand
scores.evidence: EU SAF production capacity remains well below 5% of regional jet fuel demand, notwithstanding a growing project pipeline
scores.source: IATA SAF Tracker; IEA Aviation tracking report

scores.criterion: SAF production capacity vs. jet fuel demand
scores.evidence: US SAF production capacity, while the largest in absolute terms globally, remains a small single-digit percentage of total jet fuel demand
scores.source: IATA SAF Tracker; US DOE SAF Grand Challenge tracking

scores.criterion: SAF production capacity vs. jet fuel demand
scores.evidence: China SAF production capacity is at an early stage relative to total domestic jet fuel demand
scores.source: IATA SAF Tracker; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: SAF blending mandate
scores.evidence: ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation sets a binding blending mandate starting at 2% in 2025 and escalating to 70% by 2050, with penalties for non-compliance
scores.source: EU ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation (2023/2405)

scores.criterion: SAF blending mandate
scores.evidence: US SAF policy relies on a tax credit structure rather than a binding blending mandate; no federal blending percentage requirement is in force
scores.source: US Department of Energy SAF Grand Challenge; US Treasury guidance

scores.criterion: SAF blending mandate
scores.evidence: No binding domestic SAF blending mandate identified; China participates in CORSIA on a voluntary-phase basis
scores.source: ICAO CORSIA scheme status; directional estimate on domestic mandate absence

scores.criterion: SAF price premium and corporate offtake coverage
scores.evidence: ReFuelEU mandate compliance value partially offsets the SAF premium; a growing number of corporate travel and cargo buyers have signed SAF offtake or book-and-claim agreements
scores.source: IATA SAF price tracking; airline company disclosures

scores.criterion: SAF price premium and corporate offtake coverage
scores.evidence: Federal tax credit provides a partial offset to the SAF premium; several major US airlines have signed offtake agreements, though volumes remain a small share of total fuel consumption
scores.source: Airline company disclosures; US Treasury guidance

scores.criterion: SAF price premium and corporate offtake coverage
scores.evidence: No material domestic offset mechanism or offtake agreement volume identified for the Chinese aviation market
scores.source: Directional assessment pending primary source review

scores.criterion: Dual-fuel/alternative-fuel vessel order book
scores.evidence: European-domiciled carriers have driven a material share of global methanol dual-fuel vessel orders, though the EU-flagged/owned share of the global new-build order book sits in the moderate range
scores.source: Clarksons Research World Fleet Register; DNV Alternative Fuels Insight

scores.criterion: Dual-fuel/alternative-fuel vessel order book
scores.evidence: US-flagged and US-owned share of the global alternative-fuel vessel order book remains small; the US commercial deep-sea fleet is a minor share of global tonnage
scores.source: Clarksons Research World Fleet Register; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Dual-fuel/alternative-fuel vessel order book
scores.evidence: Chinese shipyards are major builders of alternative-fuel-capable vessels for global owners, giving China a strong position in the technology supply chain even where the ordering owner is not Chinese
scores.source: Clarksons Research World Fleet Register; DNV Alternative Fuels Insight

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price / fuel intensity mandate on shipping
scores.evidence: Both EU ETS maritime inclusion (phasing in from 2024) and FuelEU Maritime's binding GHG intensity reduction targets apply concurrently, meeting the H threshold
scores.source: EU ETS Maritime Directive 2023/959; EU FuelEU Maritime Regulation 2023/1805

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price / fuel intensity mandate on shipping
scores.evidence: No US federal carbon price or fuel intensity mandate applies to shipping; US engagement with IMO measures remains at the negotiation stage
scores.source: IMO Revised GHG Strategy status; World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard

scores.criterion: Effective carbon price / fuel intensity mandate on shipping
scores.evidence: No domestic Chinese carbon price or fuel intensity mandate applies to shipping beyond IMO's global framework, which remains at an earlier implementation stage than the EU's regional measures
scores.source: IMO Revised GHG Strategy status

scores.criterion: Green shipping corridor and cargo owner offtake commitments
scores.evidence: Several green corridor initiatives involving European ports and carriers have been announced, with committed but still limited cargo volumes
scores.source: Getting to Zero Coalition Green Corridors tracker

scores.criterion: Green shipping corridor and cargo owner offtake commitments
scores.evidence: US West Coast ports participate in several announced trans-Pacific green corridor initiatives, though committed cargo volume remains at an early stage
scores.source: Getting to Zero Coalition Green Corridors tracker

scores.criterion: Green shipping corridor and cargo owner offtake commitments
scores.evidence: Chinese ports are participants in several announced green corridor initiatives on major trade routes, reflecting China's centrality to global container trade, though binding cargo commitments remain limited
scores.source: Getting to Zero Coalition Green Corridors tracker; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Battery-electric/fuel-cell truck TCO parity
scores.evidence: TCO parity for battery-electric trucks is being reached for regional/depot-based duty cycles in several EU markets, aided by lower energy costs and purchase incentives, but long-haul remains uncompetitive
scores.source: ICCT Total Cost of Ownership analyses; IEA Global EV Outlook heavy-duty chapter

scores.criterion: Battery-electric/fuel-cell truck TCO parity
scores.evidence: US TCO analyses show approaching parity for depot-based regional operations but long-haul TCO remains materially above diesel given charging infrastructure and payload constraints
scores.source: ICCT Total Cost of Ownership analyses

scores.criterion: Battery-electric/fuel-cell truck TCO parity
scores.evidence: Chinese battery-electric heavy trucks have reached TCO parity or better for depot-based and regional operations, driven by the world's lowest battery costs and government purchase subsidies
scores.source: IEA Global EV Outlook heavy-duty chapter; BloombergNEF China EV tracking

scores.criterion: Zero-emission heavy vehicle sales mandate or CO2 standard
scores.evidence: EU CO2 standards for heavy-duty vehicles set binding fleet-average reduction targets with penalties for manufacturers, among the most stringent globally
scores.source: EU Regulation 2024/1610 (heavy-duty vehicle CO2 standards)

scores.criterion: Zero-emission heavy vehicle sales mandate or CO2 standard
scores.evidence: EPA Heavy-Duty Phase 3 GHG standards are binding at the federal level, with California's Advanced Clean Fleets/Advanced Clean Trucks regulations providing additional state-level stringency, though implementation and legal challenges create some uncertainty over the assessment horizon
scores.source: US EPA Heavy-Duty Phase 3 GHG standards; California Air Resources Board

scores.criterion: Zero-emission heavy vehicle sales mandate or CO2 standard
scores.evidence: China's NEV credit system extends to commercial vehicles, creating a mandate-like mechanism, though the stringency and enforcement differs structurally from the EU/California standards
scores.source: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China) NEV credit policy

scores.criterion: Charging/refuelling infrastructure density on freight corridors
scores.evidence: EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation mandates minimum charging point density on TEN-T core network corridors, with deployment underway but not yet complete against the mandated schedule
scores.source: EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (2023/1804)

scores.criterion: Charging/refuelling infrastructure density on freight corridors
scores.evidence: Public heavy-duty charging infrastructure on long-haul freight corridors remains sparse; deployment is concentrated around depots and distribution centres rather than public highway corridors
scores.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center

scores.criterion: Charging/refuelling infrastructure density on freight corridors
scores.evidence: China has the largest absolute public charging network globally, including growing heavy-duty-capable infrastructure, though density on the most important long-haul freight corridors is uneven
scores.source: China Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Promotion Alliance

scores.criterion: Methane abatement technology deployment
scores.evidence: EU/EEA-domiciled operators (particularly North Sea producers) report among the highest LDAR and flaring-reduction technology deployment rates globally, reinforced by OGMP 2.0 reporting commitments
scores.source: IEA Methane Tracker; OGMP 2.0 reporting

scores.criterion: Methane abatement technology deployment
scores.evidence: LDAR deployment is growing under new EPA methane rules but remains uneven across operators and basins, with flaring intensity notably higher in some shale basins than in the North Sea
scores.source: IEA Methane Tracker

scores.criterion: Methane abatement technology deployment
scores.evidence: Methane monitoring and abatement technology deployment in China's upstream sector remains at an earlier stage than the EU or US based on available IEA methane intensity data
scores.source: IEA Methane Tracker; directional estimate pending primary verification

scores.criterion: Methane regulation and fee structure
scores.evidence: EU Methane Regulation establishes binding MRV requirements, leak detection and repair obligations, and an import standard applicable to non-EU suppliers from 2027
scores.source: EU Methane Regulation (2024/1787)

scores.criterion: Methane regulation and fee structure
scores.evidence: The EPA's Waste Emissions Charge implementing rule was nullified via a Congressional Review Act joint resolution (H.J.Res.35, P.L. 119-2) signed 14 March 2025. The underlying statutory fee remains on the books but EPA is barred from collecting it until 2034, and the CRA bars EPA from issuing a substantially similar rule without new legislative authority. No enforceable federal methane price currently applies to US upstream oil and gas operations; EPA performance standards (NSPS OOOOb/EG OOOOc) and GHG reporting requirements remain in effect but carry no direct cost mechanism.
scores.source: Federal Register, Congressional Review Act Revocation of Waste Emissions Charge (90 FR, 19 May 2025); Congressional Research Service R48906; Harvard Environmental & Energy Law Program regulatory tracker

scores.criterion: Methane regulation and fee structure
